newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIANS LACK HOPE TO RESOLVE CRISIS - U.N..
newsitem.headline: BULGARIANS LACK HOPE TO RESOLVE CRISIS - U.N..

text.p: Bulgarians appear to lack the hope and confidence they need to combat the country's deep economic and social crisis, a United Nations official said on Wednesday.

"I am extremely worried by the lack of hope and confidence among Bulgarian people," Antonio Vigilante, the new permanent representative of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Bulgaria, told a news conference.
"I think that the negativism and sence of hopelessness will not help Bulgarians to cope with the crisis," said Vigilante, who was appointed in August.
Thousands of people turned out for a trade union rally in Sofia on Tuesday evening to protest at the Socialist government's economic and social policies.

Fuel and bread shortages loom in the approaching winter unless the central bank can find the money for grain, nuclear fuel and coal from dwindling foreign currency reserves which fell to $506 million in September from $575 million in August.
Monthly inflation averages nearly 20 percent and the average monthly salary is now worth the equivalent of $55. Violent crime is on the increase.
In a desperate bid to stabilise the financial sector, the Bulgarian National Bank has put nine banks in receivership and raised its main interest rate to an all-time high of 300 percent annually.

The International Monetary Fund has postponed a badly-needed $115 million credit because of delays in implementing economic reforms and there are fears that Bulgaria will default on its foreign debt payments next year.
Presidential elections are due on October 27, but polls show many Bulgarians will not bother voting as they have lost faith in politicians' ability to improve their lot.
A recent poll conducted by the local branch of Gallup International showed that only 2.7 percent of Bulgarians expect the situation in the country to improve in the coming year.
